page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What they are
steps.why: They wait in the plasma doing nothing until an infection switches them on, so the body is armed without being at war.
common_mistakes: Calling them antibodies. They complement antibodies but are not antibodies.
Leaving out that they are inactive to begin with.
steps.memory_tip: They complete, or complement, the work of antibodies.
steps.margin_note: Say inactive. It is the marked word.
lines: Complement proteins are a group of
inactive plasma proteins and cell surface

steps.label: What they do
steps.why: A hole in the membrane lets fluid rush in, so the infected cell swells until it bursts.
common_mistakes: Saying they engulf microbes. They punch holes in them.
Leaving out the membrane attack complex.
steps.memory_tip: They drill pores, water rushes in, the cell bursts.
steps.margin_note: Name the complex and the result.
lines: When activated they form membrane attack
complexes, which make pores in the plasma

lines.text: Fluid enters, and the cell swells and bursts

insider_note: The marked chain is: inactive proteins, activated, membrane attack complex, pores, cell bursts. Say 'inactive' — that is what makes them complement proteins rather than antibodies.
